paragraphs.text: A small tuo of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) made in Yunnan in 1998. The leaf went through [wet piling](shou:wet-piling), heaped warm and damp so that heat and microbes could ferment it, then was steamed and pressed into its small bowl shape.
At twenty-eight years it has long since passed into what the trade counts as [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged), where storage shapes the tea as much as the years do.

brewing.text: Ease a piece off the tuo along its edge with a pick rather than snapping it. Use boiling water, about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. Old ripe tea like this gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
